steps.title: Earth's axial tilt
steps.say: Seasons are caused by Earth's tilted axis, which stays pointed in the same direction as we orbit the Sun.

steps.title: Northern winter
steps.say: In December, the Northern Hemisphere tilts away from the Sun, receiving indirect light and shorter days.

steps.title: Spring equinox
steps.say: As Earth orbits to March, neither hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, so both receive equal sunlight.

steps.title: Northern summer
steps.say: In June, the Northern Hemisphere tilts directly toward the Sun, bringing intense direct rays and summer heat.

steps.title: Autumn equinox
steps.say: By September, Earth reaches the opposite equinox, where sunlight is balanced again before heading back toward winter.

steps.title: Explore the orbit
steps.say: Now try dragging the Earth around its orbit to observe how sunlight and seasons shift across both hemispheres.
